feature.title: Track B0: DSV4.1 gate training capture for a learned L+1..L+4 predictor

brief.goal: A session-split DSV4.1 training corpus, captured on the served EXL3 fused path with the production recipe and prefetch off, that holds for every (verify forward, layer, token) the gate input, native routes and weights, the device RAM map of the next four layers at the prediction point, and each routed lane's true demand kind, with timestamps, identity, an integrity report and a manifest. It is what Track B1 (baselines, E2/E5, L+1 and L+2/L+4 evaluation) trains and tests on.
criteria: With the new env var unset, serving is unchanged: no new kernels in the captured decode graph, and the existing router-capture, spec-margin and prefetch tests pass unchanged.

On the GPU, the snapshot ring equals masks computed on the host from the same map bank for rows T+1..T+4, with boundary-crossing horizons marked invalid, and the label ring equals the host lane-typing reference.
The integrity tool exits non-zero on a non-tie route mismatch and zero on a bf16 rank-6/7 tie (counted), proven on synthetic data, and reports zero non-tie mismatches on the real corpus.
A 2-session pilot on divix01 passes the integrity tool before the full run starts.

At least 270 of 300 sampled sessions are captured complete (no seq gaps, no missing records) on /mnt/nvme1, with a manifest giving commit, recipe, the seeded whole-session split, sizes and checksums; failed and drive-flagged sessions are listed.

DSV41_REFERENCE gets a B0 entry with the corpus path, the integrity numbers (tie rate, eviction-between-snapshot-and-demand rate, failed and flagged sessions) and the capture's measured per-forward overhead.
rules: R1: Production on divix01 stays stopped; never touch cc-expert-prediction/dsv41-direct-prod.
R2: Follow .claude/rules/divix01-run-protocol.md (push/pull worktrees, taskset 0-63, locks in order, PIPESTATUS).
R3: Captures and corpora go on /mnt/nvme1, never the root volume (which holds /data) or nvme0/2/4; small reports may go under /data/models/slang/nvfp4-work/<task>/.
R4: New SGLANG_* env vars follow .claude/skills/env-var-conventions; comments follow .claude/rules/comment-style.md.
R5: Host C++ changes give every JIT module a new build key: tests that spawn children warm modules in the parent (spawn_child).
R6: No capture or test reads the mirror drives while an A/B runs; check with ps -eo cmd | grep -E "launch_server|both_cpu_ab|run_arm.sh" first.

Spec rules R1-R6 apply to every task: production on divix01 stays stopped and dsv41-direct-prod is never touched; follow .claude/rules/divix01-run-protocol.md; corpora go only on /mnt/nvme1; env vars follow env-var-conventions and comments follow comment-style.md; C++ changes mean children warm modules via spawn_child; no capture reads the mirror drives while an A/B runs.

One new switch: an EnvBool(False) on Envs in python/sglang/srt/environ.py, placed directly under SGLANG_DSV41_ROUTER_CAPTURE_PATH with a 1-2 line comment, named SGLANG_DSV41_RESIDENCY_CAPTURE unless the env-var skill forces another verb. Read it only via envs.X.get(), override it in tests with envs.X.override(). Add a matching row next to SGLANG_DSV41_ROUTER_CAPTURE_PATH in docs/docs/references/environment_variables.mdx.
Refuse the switch the way Exl3RamMissService.ensure_started refuses router capture without the trace: a RuntimeError naming both env vars when SGLANG_DSV41_ROUTER_CAPTURE_PATH is empty.

Off means absent (D2/C1): when the switch is unset, allocate no new tensor, launch nothing and add no Python call in the graph path. Copy the GraphRouteLog.enable_router/record_router pattern: rings are None until enabled, _ring() and _emit include them only when non-None, rings are allocated by a warmup forward and never during a stream capture or after the first read, and no dtype cast happens in the graph.

New rings live in GraphRouteLog (python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/exl3_stream_trace.py) on the existing slot, keyed on the existing seq/pass_id, and are read back by the same poll/_emit (one batch behind, pinned host buffers, overwrite counted in `dropped`). Their side files follow RouterCapture: raw little-endian <prefix>.<name>.bin plus fields in a .json header with a schema int. Bump ROUTER_CAPTURE_SCHEMA with a numbered comment saying what was added, and flush after every _emit.

Snapshot record layout, shared by the CUDA kernel, the host reference and the readers: per (forward, layer row T), 4 horizons x 384-bit mask (6 x uint64, bit e set iff map_bank['ram_slot'][row(T+h)][e] >= 0), a per-horizon valid flag, and a uint64 %globaltimer stamp (cuda::ptx::get_sreg_globaltimer(), as in lease_device.cuh). Label record per (forward, layer): each route's kind as uint8 in route order. LaneKind values come from ram_slot_map.LaneKind (1..5) for routes in the plan's lanes; use a new code 0 = VRAM hot for routes outside the planned lanes. Each label record also carries a %globaltimer stamp. State the layout once, in a module docstring or header comment, and reference it everywhere else.

The snapshot is launched from Exl3RamMissRowBackend.post (exl3_ram_miss.py) right after side.post, the point where the GPU scorer's spec_score runs, on the post's stream, and only when the switch is on. The label copy reads ExpertStreamDevice.lane_kind after the same post.

Device code: new kernels go in a new header under python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/moe/expert_stream/ included from moe/exl3/exl3_ram_miss.cuh and exported through a new *_METHODS dict in _device_wrappers (expert_stream_transport.py). Python wrappers validate dtype/device/contiguity as _check_buffers and run_spec_select do. Exported C++ entities get Doxygen \brief/\param.

Host reference first: pure-Python snapshot masks (from a MapReplica-shaped bank) and route labels (from type_lanes plus hot-route marking) go in python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/ram_slot_map.py or a small new sibling module. The GPU tests in test/manual/dsv41 compare the kernels against them, as test_exl3_slot_map_kernels_cuda.py does.

Keep big files from growing: exl3_ram_miss.py, expert_stream_transport.py and exl3_stream_trace.py are already large, so put new logic in new small modules and add only thin hooks to those files. Use msgspec.Struct (not @dataclass, see router_score.RouterCapture), no defensive getattr/hasattr, keyword arguments for calls of 2+ args, protected helpers by default, functions under ~100 LOC.

Driver: a new script in analysis/dsv41-drive/prefetch-replay/ (beside capture_verify.py). It reuses capture_verify/spec_margin_capture helpers by import (server_env shape, stop_server, _healthy, check_capture) and gets its env from both_cpu_ab.ARMS['dspark-both-misscut'][0] through arm_env.arm_env, plus the trace, router capture, the new switch and SGLANG_DSV41_VERIFY_ACCEPT_LOG_PATH. It takes run_locks.take(DISK_LOCK) and then run_locks.take(arm_env.GPU_LOCK), uses taskset SERVER_CORES/DRIVER_CORES and its own PORT constant, and stops the launcher with a launcher-only SIGTERM. It serves one session at a time with a DONE marker per session and drive_flags from drive_sessions.flag_sessions.

Driver refusals are pure functions tested on CPU: an output path not under /mnt/nvme1 (root volume, nvme0/2/4); SGLANG_DSV41_RAM_PREFETCH not '0'; an arm other than dspark-both-misscut; a running launch_server/both_cpu_ab/run_arm.sh (ps -eo cmd); and resolved expert_stream_requirements_for that are not EXL3. Assert the resolved format explicitly, as benchmarks/dsv41_flash check_gate does, because a non-directory model_path silently falls back to NVFP4.

Integrity and manifest tool: a new script beside router_score.py or capture_verify.py. It reuses router_score.load_capture/bf16_to_f32/load_gates and tier_sim.load_forwards, with the gate math sqrt(softplus(x@W.T)) in fp32 + bias, top-6 compared as sets. A rank-6/7 swap within bf16 rounding counts as a tie; any other mismatch is preserved in the report and makes the exit code non-zero. The manifest includes the git commit, the recipe env, the session list, the seeded whole-session split 180/45/30/45, file sizes and sha256s.

Tests: CPU tests go in existing files where the subsystem has one: test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_exl3_stream_trace.py (rings/side files), test/registered/unit/kernels/test_ram_slot_map.py (host reference), analysis/dsv41-drive/prefetch-replay/test_*.py beside the new scripts (driver, integrity tool). A new registered file calls register_cpu_ci(est_time=..., suite='base-a-test-cpu'). GPU tests go in test/manual/dsv41/*_cuda.py. Every case must pass .claude/rules/unit-test-admission.md.

Workers cannot run anything on divix01. The pilot, the full run, the overhead measurement and the integrity numbers are produced by checks. Any document that records them (the DSV41_REFERENCE.md B0 entry, a new 33.x subsection after 33.24) writes `pending` for each number; hx fills them in.

Horizon validity (owner decision): horizon_targets maps (row T, h in 1..4) to the map row whose model layer id is layer_ids[T] + h, and to -1 (invalid) only when no streamed row has that layer id. No other rule invalidates a horizon. The GPU kernel takes these precomputed targets and does not recompute validity.

Per-row header metadata: the residency side files' .json header carries one entry per map row with layer_id (the model layer), stratum (the label from stratum()) and gate_has_bias (bool: whether the layer's router gate has an e_score_correction_bias, the property ram_prefetch.prefetch_targets selects on; false for hash-routed or gateless layers). Old captures and the router .json stay readable.

Share the stratum function, do not copy it: move spec_margin.stratum's body into a new dependency-free module python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/dsv41_strata.py (stdlib only, no torch). analysis/dsv41-drive/dspark/spec_margin.py then imports it, so spec_margin.stratum stays importable and test/registered/unit/scripts/test_spec_margin.py passes unchanged. The serving header writer and the integrity/manifest readers import the same function.

items.body:
(§1 and §2 approved by the owner 2026-10-11)

### 1. Components
- Prediction-point snapshot: after layer T's post (where the score kernel runs), copy the device map bank rows T+1..T+4 (`ram_slot`, mapped if >= 0) into a ring as 384-bit masks plus a `%globaltimer` stamp. Device map, lag included, is what a GPU predictor sees. Horizons crossing a stratum boundary are marked invalid. In-flight state is host-only; with prefetch off nothing is in flight for future layers.
- Demand label: per layer, each routed lane's kind exactly as lane typing produced it (VRAM hot, RAM hit, NVMe miss, CPU-served) plus a `%globaltimer` stamp; replaces the per-layer miss count.
- Existing router capture unchanged (x bf16 [rec,40,6,5120], top-6 ids, runtime weights, seq).
- Identity: driver writes rid -> session/turn/split; the accept log gives verify position and settled count.
- Switch: one new env var, refused unless router capture is on; off by default and byte-identical when off.
- Capture driver: extends capture_verify.py / spec_margin_capture.py; dspark-both-misscut, prefetch off, ~300 sessions to /mnt/nvme1, both locks in order, quiet box.
- Integrity + manifest tool: tie-aware gate recompute (exact route sets except bf16 rank-6/7 ties, counted; other mismatches preserved and fail); snapshot/label consistency count; manifest with commit, recipe, sessions, seeded whole-session split train/dev/calib/locked-test, sizes, checksums.

### 2. Data flow, sizing and failure handling
- Per verify forward the graph writes the router record, 40 snapshot records (192 B) and 40 label records, all keyed on the existing (seq, pass_id), so they join exactly; the host drains them like the route log; a ring overrun shows as a seq gap.
- Sessions are served one at a time with a DONE marker per session (resumable); each session's drive_flags are recorded.
- Sizing: ~2.5 MB/forward (new rings ~8 KB), ~86 MB/session, ~26 GB for 300 sessions at ~40 MB/s to /mnt/nvme1.
- Sessions: seeded random sample from sessions.jsonl; whole-session split 60/15/10/15 = 180 train / 45 dev / 30 calib / 45 locked test.
- Driver refuses: output on root volume or nvme0/2/4; prefetch on; recipe not dspark-both-misscut; resolved launch requirements not EXL3; another server or A/B running.
- A session with a seq gap, missing router/label record, or live-count mismatch is marked failed, re-served once, then excluded and listed. Drive-flagged sessions are kept and marked.
- Integrity tool exits non-zero on any non-tie route mismatch; reports tie rate, eviction-between-snapshot-and-demand rate, failed and flagged sessions.
- Capture overhead means this corpus's stamps and miss rates compare only with each other, never with A/B throughput.

# Track B0: DSV4.1 gate training capture for a learned L+1..L+4 predictor

## Goal
A session-split DSV4.1 training corpus, captured on the served EXL3 fused path with the production recipe and prefetch off, that holds for every (verify forward, layer, token) the gate input, native routes and weights, the device RAM map of the next four layers at the prediction point, and each routed lane's true demand kind, with timestamps, identity, an integrity report and a manifest. It is what Track B1 (baselines, E2/E5, L+1 and L+2/L+4 evaluation) trains and tests on.

## Acceptance criteria
- With the new env var unset, serving is unchanged: no new kernels in the captured decode graph, and the existing router-capture, spec-margin and prefetch tests pass unchanged.
- On the GPU, the snapshot ring equals masks computed on the host from the same map bank for rows T+1..T+4, with boundary-crossing horizons marked invalid, and the label ring equals the host lane-typing reference.
- The integrity tool exits non-zero on a non-tie route mismatch and zero on a bf16 rank-6/7 tie (counted), proven on synthetic data, and reports zero non-tie mismatches on the real corpus.
- A 2-session pilot on divix01 passes the integrity tool before the full run starts.
- At least 270 of 300 sampled sessions are captured complete (no seq gaps, no missing records) on /mnt/nvme1, with a manifest giving commit, recipe, the seeded whole-session split, sizes and checksums; failed and drive-flagged sessions are listed.
- DSV41_REFERENCE gets a B0 entry with the corpus path, the integrity numbers (tie rate, eviction-between-snapshot-and-demand rate, failed and flagged sessions) and the capture's measured per-forward overhead.

## Decisions
- Lives in story ST8, branch `codex/dsv41-learned-predictor` from `origin/master`.
- No change to serving behaviour or production defaults: the new capture rings are opt-in by env var and absent from the graph when it is unset.
- Labels come from a new in-graph residency snapshot (option 1, owner 2026-10-11), not the job-trace join (option 2) or verify_replay's simulated tiers (option 3, 14.5% below server misses).
- The snapshot at layer T's prediction point covers target layers T+1..T+4 (H = 4, owner 2026-10-11), so the same capture supports L+1, L+2 and L+4 evaluation (handoff E3).
- Each prediction point and each layer's demand carry a GPU timestamp, so B1 can price lead time per horizon.
- Capture runs with RAM prefetch off, so speculative reads do not change the miss pattern.
- The corpus goes on `/mnt/nvme1` (414 GB free); `/data` is on the root volume (7.2 GB free) and is not used.
- Track B is split in two hx features (owner, 2026-10-11): this one is B0 (the training capture, its integrity check and manifest); B1+B2 (baselines, E2/E5 training, evaluation, verdict, §33.25) is a second feature specified once the real corpus shape is known.

## Rules
- Production on divix01 stays stopped; never touch `cc-expert-prediction/dsv41-direct-prod`.
- Follow `.claude/rules/divix01-run-protocol.md` (push/pull worktrees, taskset 0-63, locks in order, PIPESTATUS).
- Captures and corpora go on `/mnt/nvme1`, never the root volume (which holds `/data`) or nvme0/2/4; small reports may go under `/data/models/slang/nvfp4-work/<task>/`.
- New `SGLANG_*` env vars follow `.claude/skills/env-var-conventions`; comments follow `.claude/rules/comment-style.md`.
- Host C++ changes give every JIT module a new build key: tests that spawn children warm modules in the parent (`spawn_child`).
- No capture or test reads the mirror drives while an A/B runs; check with `ps -eo cmd | grep -E "launch_server|both_cpu_ab|run_arm.sh"` first.

## Non-goals
- A serving implementation of the head (a separate hx-brainstorming spec, only if B2 passes).
- Training or evaluating any predictor, baselines included (Track B1, a separate feature).
- Capturing in-flight state for future layers (host-only; empty with prefetch off).

tasks.intent: In DeepseekV4ForCausalLM.post_load_weights, widen the condition so register_moe_gates runs when SGLANG_DSV41_RAM_PREFETCH or SGLANG_DSV41_RESIDENCY_CAPTURE is on. tasks.title: Host reference: horizon targets/valid, snapshot masks, route labels
tasks.intent: New pure module residency_capture_ref.py holding the layout constants and the host reference the kernels transcribe (C2, D4). horizon_targets returns targets (the row whose layer id is layer_ids[T]+h, or -1 if there is none) and valid = target != -1. snapshot_masks writes all zeros for target -1. route_labels returns 0 for VRAM hot, otherwise the lane's LaneKind. CPU tests in test_ram_slot_map.py: crossings of Engram 1/14 and 2/15, 19->20, 21 and >=37 stay valid; past the last row is invalid and all zero; labels agree with type_lanes.

tasks.title: CUDA snapshot and label kernels
tasks.intent: New header csrc/moe/expert_stream/residency_snapshot.cuh, included from exl3_ram_miss.cuh. The snapshot kernel takes the precomputed targets and valid flags, writes the mask from ram_slot when target >= 0 (zero otherwise), copies valid, and stamps %globaltimer. The label kernel takes routes/planned/count/lane_kind and writes uint8 kinds plus a stamp. Both are exported through a new _RESIDENCY_METHODS in _device_wrappers, with validated Python wrappers.

tasks.intent: Add enable_residency(prefix, *, rows) and record_residency to GraphRouteLog, writing rings on the existing slot with index_copy_. The rings join _ring/_emit only when enabled. A new residency_capture writer/loader module handles <prefix>.snap.bin, .label.bin, .seq.bin and the .json header (schema, VALIDITY_RULE, per-row layer_id/stratum/gate_has_bias). Bump ROUTER_CAPTURE_SCHEMA. CPU tests in test_exl3_stream_trace.py cover the round trip with header, the exact (seq, pass_id) join, a gap counted as dropped, and no ring when off.
tasks.produces: ResidencyRow(msgspec.Struct, frozen): layer_id:int, stratum:str, gate_has_bias:bool; residency_rows(layer_ids, *, gates: Mapping[int, RouterGate]) -> list[ResidencyRow]; GraphRouteLog.enable_residency(prefix: str, *, rows: list[ResidencyRow]); GraphRouteLog.record_residency(row, *, masks, valid, snap_stamp, kinds, label_stamp); residency_capture.load_residency(prefix) -> ResidencyRecords(header, rows, validity_rule, masks [rec,layers,4,6] uint64, valid [rec,layers,4], snap_stamp [rec,layers], kinds [rec,layers,tokens,topk] uint8, label_stamp [rec,layers], keys [rec,3]); raises ValueError on a header without rows.

tasks.intent: When the switch is on, _start_route_log calls enable_residency (prefix: router path + '.res') with residency_rows(layer_ids, gates=registered_gates()). Each row backend gets a ResidencyHook holding staging buffers and its horizon_targets targets/valid as device tensors allocated before capture. Right after side.post the hook launches both kernels and then record_residency. When the switch is off, nothing is allocated or launched (C1, D2).

It checks the snapshot kernel against horizon_targets/snapshot_masks on a known bank, including a valid 19->20 crossing and a past-the-last-row horizon (invalid and zero). It checks the label kernel against route_labels/type_lanes. It also measures the snapshot time per layer with a working set past L2 and prints it.

tasks.title: Integrity tool: tie-aware gate recompute and consistency counts
tasks.intent: New b0_integrity.py. It recomputes the gate with router_score's math and compares route sets. A rank-6/7 bf16 tie is counted; any other mismatch is kept and makes the exit non-zero (C3). It counts seq gaps, missing router/label records and invalid (no-target) horizons. It reads the per-row header (refusing a header without it) and reports tie and eviction-between-snapshot-and-demand rates overall and per stratum, never filtering. Synthetic tests: a clean pass, a counted tie, a failing non-tie mismatch, a header without rows.

It adds per-file sizes and sha256s and the failed and drive-flagged session lists. Includes a CPU test.

It refuses an output path outside /mnt/nvme1, prefetch on, an arm other than dspark-both-misscut, a running launch_server/both_cpu_ab/run_arm.sh, and resolved expert_stream_requirements_for that are not EXL3 (asserted explicitly, as check_gate does). tasks.intent: New b0_capture.py. The env is dspark-both-misscut plus the trace, router capture, residency switch and accept log. It calls refuse_launch, takes the locks in order and serves sessions one at a time, writing rid -> session/turn/split and a DONE marker per session so a run can resume. A session that fails completeness is re-served once, then listed. drive_flags are recorded and the manifest is written at the end. CPU tests cover the env and the resume/retry bookkeeping.

tasks.title: DSV41_REFERENCE B0 entry
tasks.intent: A new 33.x B0 subsection after 33.24 (C6) covering the corpus path on /mnt/nvme1, the recipe and switch, and the record layout. It states that horizons are invalid only when they have no target row, and lists the per-row header fields (layer_id, stratum, gate_has_bias) B1 filters on. It explains how to rerun the pilot and the full run. All measured numbers are written as `pending`.

tasks.title: Residency snapshot and label kernels against their host reference
tasks.intent: T5 is T4's host reference written in CUDA, and T8 tests that the two agree (C2). One reviewer can check that all three use the same record layout and the same horizon rule.
tasks.focus: Horizon rule (owner): a horizon is invalid only when no streamed row has layer id layer_ids[T]+h. Horizons that cross Engram 1/14 and 2/15, 19->20, 21 or >=37 stay valid, and the tests must cover both sides of the rule. An invalid horizon has an all-zero mask. The kernel takes the precomputed targets and valid flags, never recomputes them, and never reads past the last row. Layout seam across residency_capture_ref, residency_snapshot.cuh and the wrappers: bit e lives in word e/64, uint64 values are read through int64 views, and the valid flag is copied, not derived. Labels: routes outside planned[:count] get 0, the others LaneKind 1..5, in route order. The %globaltimer stamp is written once per record. The wrappers validate their inputs, and the kernels can be captured in a graph. Changing the _device_wrappers exports changes the build key (R5). The timing test's working set must exceed L2.

tasks.title: Opt-in residency capture: switch, gate registration, strata, GraphRouteLog rings and header, row-post wiring
tasks.intent: These are the serving side of the capture: the switch and its refusal, the gate registration behind gate_has_bias, the shared stratum function, the rings and side files with their per-row header, the post hook, and the GPU test showing that with the switch off nothing changes. All of them are held to D2/C1: off means absent.
tasks.focus: C1/D2: with the switch unset, nothing is allocated, launched or called in post, and _ring/_emit stay byte-identical. The widened register_moe_gates condition must not change serving; it only stores references. The schema bump must keep old router captures loadable. The header carries, per row, layer_id, stratum (spec_margin.stratum imported, not copied, so test_spec_margin is unchanged) and gate_has_bias from registered_gates() (false when a gate is missing), plus VALIDITY_RULE 'invalid: no target row'. Rings are allocated in warmup, never during capture or after the first poll. record_residency uses row 0's slot, so the (seq, pass_id) join is exact and an overwrite counts as dropped. The hook's targets and valid are device tensors allocated before capture. The hook runs after side.post on the post stream and must not race the spec_score fork. ensure_started refuses the switch when router capture is off. The env-var conventions and the docs row are followed. T9's node-count assertion must actually detect an added kernel, and its children use spawn_child.

tasks.title: B0 capture driver, integrity tool, split, manifest and reference entry
tasks.intent: These are the offline tools under analysis/dsv41-drive/prefetch-replay that produce and check the corpus, plus the reference entry that documents them. They share one reading context: the on-disk format with its per-row header and validity rule, and the run protocol.
tasks.focus: C3: only a rank-6/7 swap within bf16 rounding counts as a tie. Any other mismatch is kept and exits non-zero, and so do a missing record and a seq gap. A header without rows is refused. Rates are reported per stratum, but no horizon is filtered, and invalid_no_target is counted. Check that the eviction-between-snapshot-and-demand rate is defined correctly. The manifest's per-row metadata and validity rule must be checked identical across sessions, and it must carry the checksums and the commit. Every refusal must fire, and EXL3 is asserted explicitly. Locks are taken disk first, then GPU, and only the launcher is sent SIGTERM. Resume works from DONE markers: a failing session is re-served exactly once, then listed, and drive_flags are recorded. The split is seeded, deterministic, whole-session and 180/45/30/45. The reference entry states the 'invalid only with no target row' rule and writes `pending` for every measured number.
